observation.reflection:
Verdict: NEEDS_REVISION
Issues: The current hypothesis assumes that inspecting the original image pixels will definitively resolve laterality on a lateral view; however, lateral chest X-rays are inherently poor for determining left vs. right laterality without anatomical landmarks (like the gastric bubble or heart border) which may be obscured or ambiguous in effusion cases. Relying solely on pixel inspection of a single lateral view ignores the fundamental limitation of the projection itself. Furthermore, the conflict might stem from one model misidentifying the view (e.g., confusing an AP/PA for a lateral) or misinterpreting overlapping structures (like the diaphragm or liver shadow) rather than just "difficulty" with the lateral view.
Action: Check if a corresponding PA or AP view is available in the study metadata to correlate findings, as this is the standard of care for determining laterality, rather than attempting to force a determination from the lateral view alone.
